documentation.version_scope: Locally installed HPC SDK25.5 documentation is newer than active NCU2022.4; conceptual guidance only. The2022.4 official archive was inaccessible via browsing; version-specific options require root validation.
documentation.principles: Kernel replay restores device-written memory before additional passes. Host actions are not replayed with it. Application replay repeats host work but requires deterministic kernel activities and safe output handling. Concurrent workloads can require range-aware methods; availability and capture API restrictions must be checked for installed tool.

rows.verdict_scope: kernel replay cannot preserve same-allocation CPU/GPU coexecution contract
rows.reason: GPU system atomics and CPU atomics modify the SAME managed/UnifiedMemory allocation while the device launch is outstanding. Device-only replay does not repeat host participation for every metric pass. Restoring GPU-visible state is insufficient to reconstruct CPU/device interleavings; even successful process exit is not unchanged coexecution.
rows.requirements: Do not use current multi-pass kernel replay for this contract. Separate reviewed application replay must reproduce fresh CPU execution, managed allocation and property checks each pass; kernel matching/determinism and output isolation must be reviewed. Single-pass collection is a separately declared diagnostic, not automatic approval.
rows.instrumentation_alternative: Application replay with fresh per-pass output roots; or instrument one real execution with a separately approved single-pass metric set. Keep property rather than raw atomic outcome identity.

rows.verdict_scope: static host-participation criterion only; full device memory checkpoint/restore and scientific audit required
rows.reason: All six work arrays are cudaMalloc device buffers. CPU synchronisation-flag readback and prefix sum occur BETWEEN kernel launches using blocking cudaMemcpy; no selected kernel waits for a concurrently executing host response. Phase2 convergence changes successive kernel input states, so its first invocation is only one convergence state.
rows.requirements: Require complete restoration of device-written sync_points/sizes/flags/output for each metric pass, unchanged callback stream ordering, successful final exact decode and scratch/guard CPU audits, and no profiler warnings. Source review does not prove inter-block convergence under every instrumented schedule. Inventory every phase and convergence-state role before ROI aggregation.
rows.instrumentation_alternative: Application replay if checkpoint/restore or instrumented convergence fails, preserving original loop and full audits; NVTX stages/explicit reviewed invocation selectors for phase coverage. Never replace adaptive host convergence by fixed iteration count.

rows.reason: Forward output endpoints are copied to host and synchronized before computing reverse launch geometry. CPU feedback is between launches, not a live response required by a running GPU kernel. Device buffers use cudaMalloc/CuArray rather than shared CPU atomic state.
rows.requirements: Restore all mutated device arrays before extra passes. Preserve forward result used to choose reverse threads, exact outputs/coordinates, and full independent/guard checks. Bind both direction/geometry/state roles: first-per-name-and-geometry can omit reverse if geometry collides, and cannot certify host packing/transfers.
rows.instrumentation_alternative: Reviewed direction-specific invocation/NVTX selection or application replay if restoration/output checks fail. Keep source host-feedback ROI time from original unprofiled measurements.

rows.verdict_scope: individual independent encoding kernels only; serialized profile is not concurrent pipeline performance
rows.reason: Four streams operate on disjoint 768-byte input/1024-byte output slices; pinned host input remains stable until each stream completes. No CPU worker must respond during kernel execution. Device input/output state is replayable, but serialization and cold caches remove the intended overlap.
rows.requirements: Keep each stream offset/padding case, all stream completions and full Base64 output checks. Require device-memory restore and no warnings. Do not infer concurrent four-stream throughput, transfer overlap, or whole ROI roofline from serialized first-per-geometry kernel counters.
rows.instrumentation_alternative: For overlap-sensitive questions use reviewed application/range replay supported by installed NCU, or separate CUDA timeline instrumentation. Application replay alone can still serialize selected launches; verify tool behavior rather than assume concurrency preservation.

rows.verdict_scope: selected static partition has separate host/device storage; intra-GPU spin progress remains an instrumentation caveat
rows.reason: Selected GPU flags/data are cudaMalloc/CuArray copies, distinct from CPU std::atomic/vector allocations. CPU threads do not service the GPU flag array during the selected kernel. GPU inter-block flag chaining and in-place padding require state restore; generic system-atomic source variants do not imply the selected copy shares memory.
rows.requirements: Restore entire in-place device data/flags, preserve static alpha/cut and kernel local state. Full flag/data/guard checks mandatory. Instrumentation can alter progress of spin-wait kernels, so timeout/failure remains inconclusive rather than proof of framework limitation. CPU concurrent timing cannot be inferred from kernel counters.
rows.instrumentation_alternative: Application replay if state restore/progress fails, or separate source-equivalent device-counter diagnostic explicitly excluding CPU overlap. No silent dynamic/static partition change.
